audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagreed with their own why text. Levels 2 and 3 were Skill/Kennen while whys[1] and whys[2] say she parries the poke and out-trades the mark chain; levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items read Kennen/Fiora/Kennen while whys[3], [4] and [5] all say 'nets even', 'coinflip' and 'genuinely even'.
audit.why: Riposte answers the mark chain outright in the first three levels, then the lane settles into three genuinely even stages before Kennen's two-item Zhonya's kiting pattern finally takes the last row. The packet levelChart and the mirror audit's corrected chart are identical — Fiora / Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Skill / Skill / Kennen.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped in matched pairs to that chart with ratings 3/3/5/5/5, and phases[1] through [5].why rewritten to state the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never named a single Fiora ability except Riposte, and never explained WHY Riposte is the problem — it said only 'Parries + stuns'. Lunge's on-hit application and Duelist's Dance's heal were absent.
audit.why: Riposte parries all incoming damage AND disables, and if it blocks an immobilising effect it returns a STUN. Mark of the Storm's three-stack stun is exactly such an effect, so Kennen's win condition is the thing that arms her counterattack — the mirror audit confirmed this claim is mechanically correct and left it intact on the Fiora side. Lunge applies on-hit effects, so her damage scales with attack speed and armour reads the trade wrong. Duelist's Dance restores health and gives move speed on every Vital hit.
audit.corrected: report[5].t states the immobilise-parry rule; breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d carry the 24s and what it blocks; tradeGood and dosFull[1].d state Lunge's on-hit; dontsFull[1].d states the Vital heal and the Grievous Wounds buy.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in the full layer.
audit.why: Riposte 24/22/20/18/16, Lunge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6, Bladework 11/10/9/8/7, Grand Challenge 110/90/70 against Kennen's flat 120 — she gets her second ultimate before he does, which is why the level-6 window is even rather than his.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt; dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, phases[3].why and phases[4].why now carry the 24s.

notes: The mirror audit's corrected chart and the packet levelChart agree exactly, so the five wrong rows were flipped in matched pairs to Fiora / Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Skill / Skill / Kennen. The Riposte-parries-the-stun claim in the content layer is mechanically correct (Mark of the Storm's three-stack stun is an immobilising effect, and Riposte returns a stun when it blocks one) and was left intact — it is now also stated in the full layer, which previously said only 'Parries + stuns' without ever connecting it to Kennen's actual win condition. Grand Challenge at 110s beats Slicing Maelstrom's flat 120s, so she wins the second-ultimate race; that is now on the page. No fabricated ability names found in this matchup and no suspectNames were raised.
